newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says arrests train bomber.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says arrests train bomber.

text.p: The Sri Lankan military said on Tuesday it had arrested a Tamil Tiger rebel who it claimed planted a bomb that ripped apart a packed commuter train killing nearly 60 people in July.
"We have arrested one of the people who placed one of the three bombs on the train," military spokesman Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe told reporters.
Munasinghe declined to say how many people were involved in the bombing but presented the rebel to the reporters, allowing them to question him briefly through an interpreter.

The man identified himself as Savarimuttu Loganathan from Jaffna, former stronghold of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) which is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the country's north and east.

At least 57 people were killed and more than 500 wounded when two time bombs ripped apart two coaches of a commuter train at the Dehiwela station in the suburb of Colombo on July 24. A third bomb was defused.
Loganathan told reporters he boarded the train with the bomb in a bag and placed it on a luggage rack. He got off at Dehiwela shortly before the bombs went off.
Loganathan said he joined the LTTE in 1989 and came to Colombo in 1992 to work as a barber to stay under cover.
Munasinghe said Loganathan was arrested on Monday in police raids on two LTTE safe houses in Colombo and northwestern Puttalam district.
A stock of arms and ammunition, including two disposable U.S.-made rocket launchers and 3.5 kg (eight lb) of explosives, was also recovered, he said. Several other LTTE suspects were also detained.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year.
